q: Does charcoal pig iron from Minas Gerais count as zero emissions under CBAM?
title: Charcoal pig iron and CBAM
short: Not automatically. CO2 from biomass can be rated zero only if the biomass meets the sustainability and greenhouse gas saving criteria the CBAM monitoring rules refer to; otherwise it is counted like fossil carbon. Fossil fuels, coke and carbonates in the charge still count either way.
audience: Charcoal-based pig iron producers in Minas Gerais, including the Vale do Aco steel valley, and their EU buyers

p: The CBAM monitoring rules follow the EU emissions trading rules on biomass: the emission factor of biomass is zero only where it meets the applicable criteria from EU renewable energy law. Charcoal from planted eucalyptus with documented chain of custody can qualify; charcoal of unknown origin is treated as fossil.

ol: Charcoal purchase records by supplier and plantation, with quantities and moisture.
Evidence that the wood comes from managed plantations that meet the criteria, such as certification and land-use records.
Carbon content analyses of charcoal, coke and other reductants.
Production of pig iron for the same calendar year.

p: Any coke or coal used alongside charcoal, fuel oil or gas in stoves, and CO2 from limestone or dolomite fluxes. If part of the charcoal fails the criteria, only that part is counted as fossil.
